question: Does it indicate which of the following statements in reference to factor V of Leiden is true?

options.opa: It is the resistance of factor V to the action of protein S.
options.opb: It is an acquired disorder that is associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies.
options.opc: Its presence causes a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time.
options.opd: Together with the prothrombin mutation, it constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition in our environment.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> resistance of factor V to the action of protein S -> 90% CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> increased risk of venous thromboembolism -> 85% CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> hypercoagulability -> 80% CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> not associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies -> 70% CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> does not cause a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time -> 75% CHAIN: Factor V Leiden mutation -> most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition when combined with prothrombin mutation -> 90%
enhanced_information: Factor V Leiden mutation confers resistance to the action of protein S, leading to an increased risk of venous thromboembolism and hypercoagulability. It is not associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies or a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time. When combined with the prothrombin mutation, it constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition.
analysis: Factor V Leiden mutation confers resistance to the action of protein S, leading to an increased risk of venous thromboembolism and hypercoagulability. It is not associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies or a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time. When combined with the prothrombin mutation, it constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition. Therefore, option a is the correct statement.
